rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) – Allowable Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Rent for covered units may only be raised once every 12 months by the allowable percentage set under the RSO, and certain surcharges/utility add-ons are limited or no longer permitted.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months, by allowable percentage (per annual RSO schedule)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978 that are apartments, condos/townhomes (pre-1996 tenancies), duplexes, multiple SFDs on one parcel, certain hotel/rooming house units, ADUs/JADUs, and mobile homes, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28.
rules.exemptions: Condo/townhome units with tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995 are not rent-regulated; luxury exemption available if rent on or before May 31, 1978 exceeded a threshold.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), § 151.06 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28 and if any of the following:

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit qualifies for the 'luxury exemption' based on pre-1978 rent level, or is a condo/townhome tenancy commencing after 1995

rules.conflict_note: Text notes a separate temporary rent-increase prohibition that applied from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024, which has since expired.

rules.title: RSO Legal Reasons for Eviction & Notice Filing
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO-covered units may only evict tenants for specified at-fault or no-fault reasons, and all termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within three (3) business days of service on the tenant per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (non-RSO properties)
rules.requirement: Even rental properties not covered by the RSO are subject to the city's Just Cause Ordinance, which gives tenants eviction protections and rights.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies citywide to rental units not covered under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Even if your property is not covered under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, you and your tenants have rights and responsibilities under the Just Cause Ordinance.
